title: Rav bar Shava
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He also merited to see Rav Nachman, as in Chullin 111a: Rav bar Shava happened to visit the house of Rav Nachman. They brought him boiled liver, and he did not eat. They said to Rav Nachman, "A student of the academy (a student who was your guest) is not eating." Rav Nachman said to them, "Make Shava swallow it." From this Hyman concludes that in the days of Rav Nachman he was among the students, and in the days of Rav Kahana (the teacher of Rav Ashi) and Rav Papa he was already among the great ones of the generation, as in Berakhot 19b: Rav bar Shava expounded it before Rav Kahana; they laughed at him. Rav Kahana said, "A great man has spoken a matter; do not laugh at him."
And in Moed Katan 26a: he said to Rav Kahana.
And in Bava Metzia 66b: Rav bar Shava was owed money by Rav Kahana, etc.

And in Shevuot 30b: Rav bar Shava had a lawsuit before Rav Papa; he seated him and also seated the opposing litigant. (There the reading is "bar Sharbiya," but in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is "bar Shava.")
And in Eruvin 33b: he raised an objection to Rav Pappa.
But what we find in Berakhot 14a, "Rav bar Shava happened to visit Ravina," Hyman says it should read there "Rava bar Shava," who is a later amora, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: Rashi explains gaamu le-Shava as making Shava swallow the food against his will. In the lawsuit, Rav Pappa seats both litigants; in Eruvin33b, by contrast, Rav bar Shava raises an objection. Hyman’s bar Sherevia/bar Shava reading variant and proposed later Rava bar Shava remain distinct.

Rashi on Chullin 111a explicitly explains making Shava swallow against his will. Bava Metzia 66b gives the loan involving Kahana; the creditor direction in Hyman is retained. Shevuot 30b directly names bar Sherevia and seats both litigants, while Hyman reports a bar Shava variant. His later Rava bar Shava correction remains attributed; the exact Dikdukei Soferim reading was not inspected.
